atomicClaims.statement: Men age 65 through 75 who have ever smoked should receive one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
atomicClaims.limitation: Exact pre-existing atomic statement and stable claim ID retained; source mapping freshly verified. Limited to asymptomatic previously unscreened men; not a diagnostic strategy for symptoms.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic men 65-75 with previous tobacco use and no completed abdominal aortic screen.

atomicClaims.statement: An acceptable-risk patient with an asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm should receive prompt vascular-surgery evaluation for elective repair rather than routine surveillance alone.
atomicClaims.limitation: Exact pre-existing statement/ID retained. Anatomy, life expectancy and operative risk still govern final repair selection.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable acceptable-risk men with intact fusiform AAA.

atomicClaims.statement: AAA size assessment includes the outer aneurysm wall, not just the contrast-filled lumen.
atomicClaims.limitation: CT measurements must be perpendicular to the aortic path. One directly checked society publication.

atomicClaims.statement: Growth assessment requires comparable landmarks and measurement planes.
atomicClaims.limitation: A single oblique axial value cannot establish growth against an orthogonal prior value; repeat measurement of existing images can resolve this without repeat acquisition.

atomicClaims.statement: For asymptomatic men with a 4.0-4.9-cm AAA, annual ultrasound surveillance is recommended.
atomicClaims.limitation: Not a policy for women, symptoms, rapid confirmed growth or poor ultrasound definition.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable asymptomatic men with small fusiform AAA.

atomicClaims.statement: A 3.0-3.9-cm AAA can undergo ultrasound surveillance every three years.
atomicClaims.limitation: For asymptomatic disease without a separate concerning change.

atomicClaims.statement: Six-month ultrasound surveillance applies to unrepaired AAAs at least 5.0 cm in men or 4.5 cm in women.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; do not use surveillance to defer an otherwise indicated repair assessment.

atomicClaims.statement: For women with a 4.0-4.4-cm AAA, annual ultrasound surveillance is recommended.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; symptoms or other concerning findings can change the plan.

atomicClaims.statement: An intact AAA of at least 5.0 cm in a woman warrants elective repair assessment.
atomicClaims.limitation: Recommendation strength differs by society; diameter does not override operative fitness or preferences.

atomicClaims.statement: Symptoms attributable to an intact AAA warrant repair assessment regardless of usual asymptomatic diameter thresholds.
atomicClaims.limitation: Pain attribution requires clinical assessment; no universal numeric pain or observation interval is supplied.

atomicClaims.statement: Preserve at least one internal iliac inflow when feasible during aortoiliac repair.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; describes pelvic-perfusion protection, not a universal brand or device choice.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: AAA repair involving iliac landing zones.

atomicClaims.statement: Attachment-site flow into an excluded sac represents a sealing failure.
atomicClaims.limitation: Type I origin; one directly checked specialty standard.

atomicClaims.statement: An established type I endoleak warrants prompt correction of the seal.
atomicClaims.limitation: Cuff extension requires an available healthy landing segment; complex cases may need other repair. One directly checked publication.

atomicClaims.statement: Retrograde flow from aortic side branches can fill the excluded sac.
atomicClaims.limitation: Type II physiology; other inflow sources must be assessed.

atomicClaims.statement: An isolated type II endoleak with stable sac size can undergo imaging follow-up.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single publication; requires exclusion of higher-pressure leaks and continued surveillance.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with stable post-EVAR sac.

atomicClaims.statement: Sac enlargement with uncertain leak origin requires investigation for occult type I or III inflow.
atomicClaims.limitation: Catheter angiography with possible cone-beam CT can resolve inconclusive CTA; no disputed growth cutoff is taught.

atomicClaims.statement: Separated modular components can directly pressurize the excluded sac.
atomicClaims.limitation: Type IIIa mechanism; not retrograde branch flow.

atomicClaims.statement: A bridging graft can close a component gap causing a type III endoleak.
atomicClaims.limitation: Prompt repair is indicated; anatomy determines the precise device or need for open conversion. One checked publication.

atomicClaims.statement: A stable patient with suspected ruptured AAA can undergo urgent CT for repair planning.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; do not extend imaging delay to a patient who cannot remain stable.

atomicClaims.statement: EVAR is recommended for ruptured AAA when anatomy is suitable.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; requires specialist capability, access and device suitability, not diameter alone.

atomicClaims.statement: Ascending aortic involvement establishes type A dissection even with a distal entry tear.
atomicClaims.limitation: Classification depends on extent, not simply the tear location.

atomicClaims.statement: Acute type A dissection requires emergency surgical evaluation and immediate repair.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked multisociety guideline. This draft does not rank contested mesenteric-first strategies.

atomicClaims.statement: Uncomplicated acute type B dissection initially receives medical therapy and close monitoring.
atomicClaims.limitation: High-risk morphology and later complications can change the plan; does not ban elective later TEVAR.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Acute descending dissection without rupture or malperfusion.

atomicClaims.statement: Use intravenous beta blockade first, adding intravenous vasodilation if pressure remains high.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single directly checked recommendation; contraindications can favor a non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. No dose or numeric target is authored.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Hypertensive acute aortic syndrome without beta-blocker contraindication.

atomicClaims.statement: Acute type B dissection with organ malperfusion warrants intervention, commonly TEVAR when suitable.
atomicClaims.limitation: Static branch disease can require adjuncts; no automatic bowel resection or non-aneurysm ischemia objective is included.

atomicClaims.statement: Sealing a dissection entry can expand the true lumen and relieve dynamic branch obstruction.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single current specialty standard; response must be reassessed.

atomicClaims.statement: Persistent fixed branch narrowing after central true-lumen expansion may require branch stenting.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single specialty standard; the case supplies persistent gradient and flap extension rather than assuming every residual image needs treatment.

atomicClaims.statement: Planned left-subclavian coverage should account for a patent LIMA coronary graft by preserving its inflow.
atomicClaims.limitation: Elective setting with native landing zones; bypass versus transposition depends on anatomy.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: TEVAR involving LSA with LIMA-dependent myocardium.

atomicClaims.statement: Carotid-subclavian transposition requires temporary proximal subclavian clamping.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; the anatomy-specific interruption matters for a pedicled LIMA.

atomicClaims.statement: A patent pedicled LIMA coronary graft favors bypass over subclavian transposition to avoid interrupting coronary inflow.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline, section on LSA revascularization; other bypass/endovascular configurations remain specialist decisions.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: LSA revascularization with a patent pedicled LIMA.

atomicClaims.statement: New spinal-cord dysfunction after TEVAR calls for perfusion rescue, including pressure support and CSF drainage assessment.
atomicClaims.limitation: Rapid specialist response; drainage contraindications must be checked. No invented target, timing, guaranteed recovery or routine prophylactic drain rule.

atomicClaims.statement: A small PAA with thrombus and distal embolic findings merits repair consideration despite being below 20 mm.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single guideline, weak recommendation/low-quality evidence; excludes acutely threatened limbs requiring an ischemia-specific pathway.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: PAA under 20 mm with embolic findings.

atomicClaims.statement: Finding a PAA warrants screening the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single guideline, strong recommendation/moderate evidence; this is aneurysm screening, not broad asymptomatic arterial-stenosis screening.

atomicClaims.statement: A symptomatic expanding excluded PAA sac may require decompression despite a patent bypass.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single guideline; exclude graft failure and venous thrombosis as the cause of symptoms.

atomicClaims.statement: Unexplained infection or gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic grafting warrants cross-sectional graft evaluation.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single guideline; imaging and cultures are interpreted together, and an unrevealing endoscopy does not assess the graft.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Prosthetic aortic graft with unexplained infection/bleeding.

atomicClaims.statement: An operable stable patient with aortic graft infection can undergo graft source-control surgery and arterial reconstruction.
atomicClaims.limitation: Specific reconstruction and antimicrobial regimen need specialist judgment; endovascular bridging or suppression may fit other patients.

atomicClaims.statement: Open repair is preferred for an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; does not preclude endovascular rescue or exceptional high-risk situations. Newer ESVS full text was inaccessible.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Fit patient with heritable native-aorta TAAA.

atomicClaims.statement: Pancreatitis can disrupt an adjacent artery and produce a contained arterial leak.
atomicClaims.limitation: One CC BY specialty standard. The synthetic image observations are not a copied figure.

atomicClaims.statement: Visceral pseudoaneurysms generally warrant prompt treatment rather than true-aneurysm size surveillance.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single standard; small intraparenchymal lesions can be exceptions. This case is an extraparenchymal splenic-artery wall defect; exact true-aneurysm thresholds remain withheld.

atomicClaims.statement: A scan ending near the celiac origin does not assess the infrarenal abdominal aorta.
atomicClaims.limitation: Underlying aortic segment relationships independently synthesized from the official anatomy/segment definitions; no figure copied.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Interpreting the inferior boundary of a thoracoabdominal acquisition.

atomicClaims.statement: Repair may be reasonable after confirmed AAA growth of at least 0.5 cm in six months.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single guideline; measurements must be comparable and confirmed. This is not an automatic operation rule.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Unruptured AAA with verified serial enlargement.

atomicClaims.statement: An inadequately visualized AAA needs cross-sectional surveillance; MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline. A prior adequate ultrasound does not validate a later incomplete examination. Modality and protocol still require clinical planning.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: AAA surveillance with inadequate ultrasound definition.

atomicClaims.statement: Acute aortic-syndrome therapy generally targets a heart rate of 60-80 beats per minute while maintaining organ perfusion.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; individual perfusion and contraindications govern treatment. No dose is taught.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Monitored hospital treatment of acute aortic syndrome.

atomicClaims.statement: Intravenous nicardipine is an antihypertensive vasodilator that can be combined with beta blockade under monitoring.
atomicClaims.limitation: The regulatory label verifies pharmacology; ACC/AHA establishes adding vasodilation after initial beta blockade when pressure remains uncontrolled. No dose or infusion-rate rule is authored.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Hospital blood-pressure treatment after initial impulse control.

atomicClaims.statement: ACC/AHA recommends repair for women with AAA at least 5.0 cm, whereas the SVS summary suggests repair at 5.0-5.4 cm.
atomicClaims.limitation: The sources use different recommendation strength. This comparison supports referral for assessment in the draft, not mandatory repair for every woman or selection of a particular procedure.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Women with intact AAA being considered for elective repair.

atomicClaims.statement: An intravenous non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker is a reasonable acute aortic-syndrome rate-control alternative when beta blockers are contraindicated or not tolerated.
atomicClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline. This is a rate-control alternative, not evidence that switching from tolerated beta blockade is preferred for persistent pressure elevation after rate control.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Acute aortic syndrome with a beta-blocker contraindication or intolerance.

explanation.text: The celiac-level endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta unexamined. Apply the screening recommendation to the actual coverage, not the examination's title: abdominal ultrasound is the initial preventive screen for this eligible former smoker.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic ultrasound
choices.rationale: The prior acquisition stops above the infrarenal aorta. His age and former smoking history still support an abdominal screen.
choices.temptation: Recognizes that part of the abdominal aorta on a chest scan is not a completed infrarenal survey.
choices.counterfactual: A prior adequate abdominal acquisition documenting the full infrarenal aorta would support no additional one-time screen.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic CT angiography
choices.rationale: His record requires a first preventive abdominal screen, not detailed repair or acute-symptom anatomy; ultrasound is the supported initial modality.
choices.temptation: Extends the prior CTA technique to the unexamined lower segment because it offers more detail.
choices.counterfactual: New aneurysm-attributable symptoms would change the task to diagnostic cross-sectional imaging.

choices.label: Arrange no additional aortic imaging
choices.rationale: The study's caudal endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta outside the acquisition. Smoking cessation does not negate the ever-smoker screening indication.
choices.temptation: Counts a study labeled aortic CTA as covering the entire aorta.
choices.counterfactual: A documented adequate full infrarenal study could make another screening examination unnecessary.

explanation.text: The reported 0.7-cm difference spans different measurement planes. Use the adequate acquired volumes to establish a matched comparison before interpreting growth. Confirmed enlargement of that amount over six months could change repair assessment, so the discrepancy should not simply be deferred to routine surveillance.

choices.label: Reconstruct the serial CT volumes for matched measurements
choices.rationale: The apparent increase uses different planes. Adequate source volumes permit a valid comparison before using enlargement to determine repair assessment.
choices.temptation: Separates a changed number from established biological growth.
choices.counterfactual: Comparable orthogonal measurements confirming the same change over six months could support vascular repair evaluation.

choices.label: Refer for repair evaluation based on serial enlargement
choices.rationale: The amount and interval would matter if the measurements were comparable, but the plane discrepancy prevents treating the reported difference as confirmed growth.
choices.temptation: Correctly recognizes a potentially important rate but assumes the two report values are interchangeable.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed increase from 4.6 to 5.3 cm using the same reproducible method over six months makes repair evaluation reasonable.

choices.label: Schedule ultrasound follow-up using the latest reported size
choices.rationale: Applying a surveillance band to the unreconciled latest value does not resolve whether a consequential interval change occurred.
choices.temptation: Uses the current diameter band while overlooking a potentially important but unvalidated trajectory.
choices.counterfactual: Once comparable imaging establishes a stable unrepaired male AAA near the repair threshold, six-month ultrasound may be appropriate.

explanation.text: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. Cross-sectional assessment is needed when the sac is not defined, and MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated. The earlier matched measurements do not establish the current sac size after an inadequate examination.

choices.label: MRI of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The current ultrasound does not define full sac size; MRI provides cross-sectional assessment without requiring the iodinated-contrast exposure implicated in his prior reaction.
choices.temptation: Uses current test adequacy and the actual previous contrast response rather than reusing a formerly adequate modality.
choices.counterfactual: If the full sac were visualized reproducibly on the current ultrasound, ultrasound surveillance would remain appropriate.

choices.label: CT angiography of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.
choices.temptation: Correctly escalates imaging after an incomplete study but ignores the acquisition-specific constraint.
choices.counterfactual: Without an important CT contraindication, CT is a supported way to define an inadequately visualized AAA.

choices.label: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.
choices.temptation: Applies the ordinary small-AAA modality without checking whether this examination can actually measure the sac.
choices.counterfactual: An adequate current acoustic window and complete outer-wall visualization support ultrasound follow-up.

explanation.text: The pain pattern and focal tenderness make the aneurysm clinically concerning even though MR imaging shows no extravasation. The unchanged lumbar finding does not by itself explain this new syndrome. Inpatient vascular repair assessment is appropriate; a size-based asymptomatic surveillance rule does not settle this admission.

choices.label: Inpatient vascular assessment for aneurysm repair
choices.rationale: New focal aortic tenderness and persistent nonmechanical pain change the previously asymptomatic premise despite an intact image and smaller diameter.
choices.temptation: Interprets current symptom localization rather than treating an intact sac as necessarily asymptomatic.
choices.counterfactual: A demonstrated nonaneurysmal mechanical pain syndrome with no aortic tenderness could support a spine-directed plan and aneurysm surveillance.

choices.label: Inpatient lumbar MRI before vascular assessment
choices.rationale: The unchanged structural spine finding does not establish that it explains the new rest pain and focal pain reproduced over the aorta.
choices.temptation: Anchors on a visible spinal abnormality and delays the aortic assessment.
choices.counterfactual: New focal mechanical or neurologic findings corresponding to a new spinal lesion would strengthen a spine-directed investigation.

choices.label: Clinical observation with scheduled aortic ultrasound follow-up
choices.rationale: Routine observation and surveillance do not address the new aneurysm-localized symptoms simply because the scan shows no leak.
choices.temptation: Continues the prior small-AAA policy after interpreting intact imaging as reassurance.
choices.counterfactual: If the pain resolved with a clearly supported separate cause and aortic symptoms were absent, size-based follow-up could again be appropriate.

explanation.text: Use the maximum outer-wall sac dimension. ACC/AHA recommends repair at the female size boundary, while SVS frames repair in the 5.0-5.4-cm range as a suggestion; both support specialist repair assessment in this supplied context. Neither diameter nor sex selects a procedure or removes the need to consider operative risk and patient goals.

choices.label: Arrange elective vascular repair assessment
choices.rationale: The full outer contour, not the flowing channel, reaches the female repair-assessment range. This supports evaluation rather than choosing an operation automatically.
choices.temptation: Integrates which dimension matters with the population-specific recommendation.
choices.counterfactual: A smaller full sac could instead support continued surveillance.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in six months
choices.rationale: This can follow a male threshold applied to the full sac or a surveillance-only policy, but it postpones the supported female repair assessment here.
choices.temptation: Uses the familiar male boundary despite correctly reading the outer dimension.
choices.counterfactual: For an asymptomatic man with the same 5.1-cm full sac, six-month surveillance can be appropriate.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in twelve months
choices.rationale: The 4.2-cm flowing channel is not the aneurysm's full dimension used for the female surveillance band.
choices.temptation: Applies the correct female interval to the wrong measured structure.
choices.counterfactual: An asymptomatic woman whose full sac, rather than flowing channel, measures 4.2 cm could have annual ultrasound.

explanation.text: The current imaging leaves the right internal iliac as the remaining direct pelvic inflow. Preserve that route as part of exclusion planning when feasible. This is a strategy decision: the scan does not by itself establish eligibility for a particular iliac branch device, and the final preserving reconstruction requires separate anatomic planning.

choices.label: Preserve right internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: The right internal iliac is the remaining direct pelvic inflow. An exclusion strategy should preserve it when feasible rather than intentionally eliminating that route.
choices.temptation: Maps the opacified vessel and planned exclusion to the remaining pelvic supply.
choices.counterfactual: If the right side were occluded and the left internal iliac supplied the pelvis, left-sided preservation would be the relevant goal.

choices.label: Preserve left internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: The left channel is already occluded; assigning preservation to that side does not protect the patent right pelvic supply from the planned coverage.
choices.temptation: Reverses the side or counts a formerly named artery as current patent inflow.
choices.counterfactual: A patent left internal iliac with an occluded right side would make left-sided preservation the appropriate goal.

choices.label: Exclude both internal-iliac origins during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: This would intentionally interrupt the remaining right-sided route instead of preserving at least one direct hypogastric inflow when feasible.
choices.temptation: Prioritizes a simple distal exclusion configuration and relies on unspecified collateral compensation.
choices.counterfactual: When both direct routes are already lost or preserving inflow is truly infeasible, the clinical team must consider a different risk/strategy balance rather than assuming this draft's preserving reconstruction.

explanation.text: Delayed branch-associated flow with an unchanged sac supports continued surveillance. A visible leak is not enough to choose its treatment; source and sac behavior matter.

choices.label: Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
choices.rationale: The branch origin and unchanged sac support observation with continued imaging.
choices.temptation: Interprets both the leak route and sac behavior.
choices.counterfactual: A direct attachment leak or a growing sac would require a different evaluation or intervention.

choices.label: Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
choices.rationale: A visible branch leak does not by itself establish a treatment benefit when the sac is stable.
choices.temptation: Treats persistence of any contrast outside the graft as a repair indication.
choices.counterfactual: A persistent proven branch leak with consequential sac growth can merit embolization after other sources are excluded.

choices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
choices.rationale: The observed inflow is from lumbar branches, not the proximal attachment.
choices.temptation: Confuses every leak with a proximal seal failure.
choices.counterfactual: A proximal attachment leak with a usable extra landing segment would favor cuff extension.

explanation.text: Do not carry forward a branch-leak label when a growing sac has an uncertain current inflow source. Problem-solving aortography can assess the attachments and modular junctions before choosing a branch-directed treatment.

choices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
choices.rationale: The enlarging sac and uncertain source require reassessment for direct graft or attachment inflow before targeting a branch.
choices.temptation: Questions whether the old branch label explains the current growth.
choices.counterfactual: A clearly established enlarging isolated branch leak could move directly to targeted branch mapping and embolization.

choices.label: Selective mesenteric-to-inferior-mesenteric collateral angiography
choices.rationale: This maps a branch route but does not resolve the possible attachment or component defect producing the current sac growth.
choices.temptation: Extends the previous type-II attribution to a new scan without validating it.
choices.counterfactual: Proven inferior-mesenteric branch inflow into a growing sac can justify this approach.

choices.label: Selective iliolumbar-to-lumbar collateral angiography
choices.rationale: The lumbar branch near the contrast focus does not establish that it is the only source.
choices.temptation: Anchors on the branch seen on the earlier surveillance images.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed isolated lumbar leak with sac growth can be mapped for targeted embolization.

explanation.text: The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.

choices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
choices.rationale: A fabric gap provides a direct route into the sac. A covered bridge restores the missing barrier between the aligned components.
choices.temptation: Uses the observed mechanical defect to select a repair that actually excludes the channel.
choices.counterfactual: If the components still overlapped and the problem were remediable incomplete expansion, balloon remodelling could be appropriate.

choices.label: Balloon remodelling at the modular junction
choices.rationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.
choices.temptation: Treats every junctional leak as incomplete expansion of an existing overlap.
choices.counterfactual: An intraoperative leak from incomplete expansion within a maintained overlap can be treated by balloon remodelling.

choices.label: Bare-metal stent reinforcement at the leaking segment
choices.rationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.
choices.temptation: Confuses mechanical support with reconstruction of the exclusion barrier.
choices.counterfactual: Selected attachment-apposition leaks can use bare-metal reinforcement as an adjunct when the covered fabric and sealing anatomy are present.

explanation.text: This arterial-phase attachment route represents a type I sealing failure. Prompt seal repair is appropriate even before the sac enlarges; the available healthy neck makes proximal extension a supported option.

choices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
choices.rationale: Direct attachment inflow requires prompt seal correction; the remaining healthy segment supports a cuff.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes a sealing defect from a stable branch leak.
choices.counterfactual: Absent a usable neck, a more complex reconstruction would need consideration.

choices.label: Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
choices.rationale: Stable sac size does not justify observation of an established late direct attachment leak.
choices.temptation: Overgeneralizes conservative care for stable type-II flow.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed isolated branch leak with stable sac size supports surveillance.

choices.label: Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
choices.rationale: The demonstrated source is the proximal attachment, not a side branch.
choices.temptation: Treats contrast in the sac as a branch-leak problem regardless of its observed source.
choices.counterfactual: A growing isolated branch leak could support branch/sac embolization.

explanation.text: Use the current serial perfusion observations, not the initial pressure in isolation. At this recorded point urgent CT can define rupture and repair anatomy while definitive aortic care is prepared. Persistent or renewed circulatory collapse would change that balance toward immediate aortic control.

choices.label: Urgent CT angiography during aortic-team preparation
choices.rationale: Repeated preserved pressure and mentation after initial resuscitation support urgent cross-sectional repair planning rather than another detection-only examination.
choices.temptation: Uses the current trajectory instead of classifying the patient solely from the first low reading.
choices.counterfactual: A renewed collapse or inability to sustain perfusion would make a direct hemorrhage-control pathway appropriate instead.

choices.label: Direct operating-room transfer for open aortic control
choices.rationale: Immediate control can be necessary in collapse, but the current serial observations support obtaining repair-planning CT first.
choices.temptation: Treats an initially low pressure and large aneurysm as proof that planning imaging is no longer possible.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent deterioration in circulation despite initial resuscitation would favor proceeding to hemorrhage control rather than delaying for CT.

choices.label: Further resuscitation before any cross-sectional planning
choices.rationale: The record already shows restored mentation and sustained pressure over repeated assessments; further normalizing physiology before defining the repair anatomy unnecessarily postpones the next supported step.
choices.temptation: Waits for entirely normal vital signs rather than judging whether current perfusion permits urgent planning.
choices.counterfactual: If perfusion remained inadequate for safe movement to CT, immediate resuscitation alongside a hemorrhage-control plan would be necessary.

explanation.text: Ascending involvement determines the type-A pathway even when the entry tear is distal. Stable current pressure does not remove the need for emergency surgical treatment of acute ascending dissection.

choices.label: Emergency open ascending aortic repair
choices.rationale: Ascending involvement places this in the type-A pathway despite a descending entry tear.
choices.temptation: Classifies by the involved segment and applies its urgent surgical consequence.
choices.counterfactual: A flap confined distal to the left subclavian without complications would favor initial medical treatment.

choices.label: Urgent descending thoracic endovascular repair
choices.rationale: Treating the distal tear as a type-B problem does not address the acute ascending involvement.
choices.temptation: Classifies the dissection by the tear location alone.
choices.counterfactual: A complicated dissection confined to the descending aorta with suitable anatomy can favor TEVAR.

choices.label: Intravenous esmolol with CT angiographic follow-up
choices.rationale: Impulse control is background stabilization but not definitive treatment of acute ascending dissection.
choices.temptation: Uses normotension and absence of malperfusion to choose an uncomplicated type-B pathway.
choices.counterfactual: An uncomplicated dissection confined to the descending aorta initially receives medical therapy and monitoring.

explanation.text: Rate and pressure are separate treatment targets. The observed rate response is within the guideline range, while pressure remains elevated. Add an intravenous vasodilator after initial beta blockade rather than simply intensifying rate reduction or substituting another rate-control agent. Nicardipine provides additional blood-pressure reduction while beta blockade continues.

choices.label: Add intravenous nicardipine infusion
choices.rationale: Rate has entered the guideline target range while pressure remains uncontrolled; added vasodilation addresses the remaining treatment target after beta blockade.
choices.temptation: Separates the achieved chronotropic response from the persisting pressure problem.
choices.counterfactual: If heart rate remained markedly elevated before adequate beta blockade, further beta-blocker titration could precede vasodilation.

choices.label: Increase the intravenous esmolol infusion
choices.rationale: Escalating rate-slowing therapy does not best address the remaining pressure target once the recorded rate response is adequate and perfusion is preserved.
choices.temptation: Uses one infusion to pursue both goals without interpreting which goal has already responded.
choices.counterfactual: Persisting sinus tachycardia with tolerable perfusion and no limiting response could support further beta-blocker titration.

choices.label: Replace esmolol with intravenous diltiazem
choices.rationale: The record does not demonstrate beta-blocker intolerance or a rate-control failure requiring substitution; it shows persisting pressure elevation after a rate response.
choices.temptation: Treats incomplete pressure response as failure of the chosen rate-control drug class.
choices.counterfactual: A genuine beta-blocker contraindication or intolerance can favor a nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker for rate control.

explanation.text: Protect the pedicled LIMA coronary inflow before elective LSA coverage. Bypass avoids the proximal subclavian clamp required for transposition; waiting for arm ischemia also fails to protect this coronary-dependent territory.

choices.label: Carotid-subclavian bypass before aortic coverage
choices.rationale: LSA interruption threatens inflow to the patent LIMA graft supplying an occluded native LAD territory.
choices.temptation: Follows the coronary conduit back to its inflow origin.
choices.counterfactual: If no LSA-dependent coronary or other critical inflow existed, timing and need could differ, particularly in an emergency.

choices.label: Aortic coverage, then bypass if arm ischemia develops
choices.rationale: An arm-symptom trigger does not protect the LIMA-dependent coronary circulation during elective coverage.
choices.temptation: Treats upper-extremity symptoms as the only meaningful consequence of LSA interruption.
choices.counterfactual: Selective delayed revascularization may fit some emergency coverings without critical LSA-dependent inflow.

choices.label: Carotid-subclavian transposition before aortic coverage
choices.rationale: Transposition requires proximal subclavian clamping, which can interrupt the patent pedicled LIMA coronary inflow; bypass avoids that required interruption.
choices.temptation: Chooses a durable LSA revascularization while overlooking its proximal clamp sequence.
choices.counterfactual: Without a patent pedicled LIMA or another clamp-dependent inflow, transposition can be a reasonable LSA revascularization technique.

explanation.text: Bilateral leg weakness after hypotension with preserved limb pulses raises concern for spinal-cord ischemia. Activate perfusion rescue and specialist CSF-drainage assessment; the new phase calls for restoring cord perfusion rather than intensifying impulse reduction.

choices.label: Vasopressor-supported perfusion with CSF-drainage rescue
choices.rationale: The pattern points to spinal-cord perfusion injury; pressure support and reduction of intrathecal pressure address that mechanism.
choices.temptation: Links bilateral motor findings with the hypotensive trigger and preserved limb inflow.
choices.counterfactual: A focal cerebral syndrome or arterial inflow loss would require a different rescue target.

choices.label: Esmolol-based pressure reduction with intravenous analgesia
choices.rationale: Further pressure reduction would work against perfusion rescue in this new postoperative neurologic syndrome.
choices.temptation: Carries an acute aortic impulse-reduction plan into a phase where low pressure is the precipitating problem.
choices.counterfactual: An unrepaired hypertensive acute aortic syndrome without cord hypoperfusion supports impulse control.

choices.label: Heparin anticoagulation with urgent aortoiliac thrombectomy
choices.rationale: Warm feet and preserved pulses make aortoiliac occlusion a poorer explanation than spinal perfusion injury.
choices.temptation: Interprets leg weakness after endovascular repair as an access or limb-occlusion complication.
choices.counterfactual: Sudden cold pulseless legs with demonstrated aortoiliac occlusion could require this pathway.

explanation.text: Digital occlusions with a thrombus-containing PAA support distal embolization even when pedal pulses remain palpable. The complication warrants vascular repair planning below the usual asymptomatic size boundary. This selects repair versus medication/surveillance; conduit assessment and anatomy determine the eventual open or endovascular technique.

choices.label: Plan popliteal aneurysm repair with vascular surgery
choices.rationale: Repeated digital embolic findings and mural thrombus support aneurysm source repair consideration despite a diameter below 20 mm.
choices.temptation: Uses the complication rather than size alone to choose the treatment strategy.
choices.counterfactual: A small asymptomatic lesion without thrombus or embolic findings can instead undergo surveillance.

choices.label: Start anticoagulation with popliteal duplex follow-up
choices.rationale: This addresses thrombotic risk without removing the demonstrated aneurysmal source. The supported strategy includes repair assessment rather than relying on medication as the definitive plan.
choices.temptation: Treats the embolic consequence without changing the persisting source.
choices.counterfactual: Prohibitive repair risk or an unavoidable treatment delay may require an interim specialist-directed medical strategy.

choices.label: Continue annual popliteal duplex surveillance
choices.rationale: The asymptomatic small-aneurysm policy does not address repeated embolic complications in this record.
choices.temptation: Lets the 18-mm diameter and palpable pedal pulses override the digital arterial findings.
choices.counterfactual: A small stable asymptomatic PAA without thrombus/embolism can be monitored.

explanation.text: Screening associated with a PAA includes the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta. The acquired left-leg study documents venous compression and flow; that reassuring result does not assess the contralateral arterial target. The abdominal CTA already supplies the aortic component of this survey.

choices.label: Left popliteal arterial duplex ultrasound
choices.rationale: The left-leg examination evaluates veins, not a contralateral arterial aneurysm; the abdominal aorta is already adequately depicted.
choices.temptation: Separates a reassuring examination at the wrong vascular target from the associated arterial survey still needed.
choices.counterfactual: An adequate left arterial examination with an unassessed abdominal aorta would instead support abdominal aortic screening.

choices.label: Abdominal aortic duplex ultrasound
choices.rationale: This is an appropriate associated site but does not address the remaining arterial target after an adequate abdominal CTA.
choices.temptation: Recalls the AAA association while mistaking the left venous examination for a completed left arterial survey.
choices.counterfactual: An abdominal acquisition that omitted the infrarenal aorta would make a dedicated aortic study appropriate.

choices.label: Thoracic aortic CT angiography
choices.rationale: A thoracic study does not complete the specifically supported opposite-popliteal and abdominal-aortic associated survey.
choices.temptation: Generalizes aneurysm association to another arterial territory while treating the recorded left-leg study as sufficient.
choices.counterfactual: An independent thoracic or heritable-aortopathy indication can justify thoracic imaging.

explanation.text: Prosthetic aortic history, unexplained bloodstream infection and bleeding raise a linked vascular concern. Cross-sectional assessment is appropriate even when a proximal mucosal examination is unrevealing. Distal enteroscopy offers a real new luminal target, but that target does not substitute for evaluating the reconstruction and extraluminal findings.

choices.label: Multiphase abdominal CT angiography
choices.rationale: The combination of prosthetic aortic history, unexplained bacteremia and bleeding calls for cross-sectional vascular and extraluminal assessment.
choices.temptation: Interprets the infection/bleeding link before choosing the test's acquisition scope.
choices.counterfactual: A clearly localized mucosal source without graft-related concern could instead favor directed endoscopic evaluation.

choices.label: Push enteroscopy into the distal duodenum
choices.rationale: This is a genuine new mucosal target beyond the previous examination, but it does not replace cross-sectional evaluation of the prosthetic reconstruction and surrounding infection concern.
choices.temptation: Correctly recognizes the prior endoscopy's limited reach but treats the remaining problem as mucosal bleeding alone.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent bleeding localized to a distal-duodenal mucosal lesion without an unresolved prosthetic-infection concern could support this investigation.

choices.label: Tagged-red-cell gastrointestinal bleeding scintigraphy
choices.rationale: Localization of intermittent bleeding does not characterize the prosthetic/infectious interface that links the other observations.
choices.temptation: Selects a bleeding-localization pathway without integrating the persistent bloodstream findings and aortic history.
choices.counterfactual: Intermittent bleeding with graft pathology adequately excluded may require a separate localization pathway.

explanation.text: For an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome, the checked multisociety guideline favors open repair. Native-aortic tissue disease and long-term durability matter even when branched or hybrid reconstruction is technically possible.

choices.label: Open thoracoabdominal graft replacement
choices.rationale: Heritable native-aorta disease in an operable patient favors open reconstruction when repair is required.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes the tissue disease from an ordinary degenerative aneurysm.
choices.counterfactual: Severe operative prohibitions or emergency bridging needs can change the balance.

choices.label: Branched endovascular thoracoabdominal repair
choices.rationale: Technical feasibility does not erase the guideline preference for open repair in this heritable native-aorta setting.
choices.temptation: Generalizes the lower initial invasiveness of endovascular repair to all aneurysm substrates.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriate degenerative TAAA patient with higher open risk may be considered for branched repair.

choices.label: Visceral debranching with thoracic endografting
choices.rationale: A hybrid operation still relies on endograft sealing in the diseased native aorta rather than providing the preferred open reconstruction.
choices.temptation: Assumes adding open visceral bypasses resolves the native-seal concern.
choices.counterfactual: Selected patients unsuitable for conventional open repair can require alternative hybrid strategies.

atomicClaims.statement: Men age 65 through 75 who have ever smoked should receive one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
atomicClaims.limitation: This claim is limited to asymptomatic men with a smoking history and no prior screening; it does not define screening for other populations.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic men age 65-75 who have ever smoked and have not previously undergone AAA screening.

atomicClaims.statement: An acceptable-risk patient with an asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm should receive prompt vascular-surgery evaluation for elective repair rather than routine surveillance alone.
atomicClaims.limitation: Anatomy and specialist assessment determine open versus endovascular repair. Pain or suspected rupture requires emergency care rather than this outpatient pathway.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable acceptable-risk men with a newly identified asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform AAA and no rupture features.

atomicClaims.statement: Contemporary pooled and national-registry evidence reports higher observed perioperative mortality among women than men after elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
atomicClaims.limitation: The evidence is derived primarily from observational cohorts and pooled observational estimates; it supports an association rather than a causal or patient-specific prediction.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm; the approved concept is limited to counseling about population-level perioperative outcomes.

atomicClaims.statement: Higher observed perioperative mortality among women has been reported after both endovascular and open elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
atomicClaims.limitation: Effect estimates and contributing mechanisms vary across cohorts, anatomy, repair approach, era, and adjustment methods; the claim does not compare an individual patient's suitability for EVAR versus open repair.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving elective EVAR or open repair for intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.

atomicClaims.statement: A sex-associated difference in population-level operative outcomes informs counseling and risk assessment but does not determine an individual patient's outcome or make female sex a contraindication to repair.
atomicClaims.limitation: Individual risk still depends on anatomy, comorbidity, repair approach, center experience, and other patient-specific factors not taught by this concept.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Learners interpreting observed sex-associated AAA repair outcomes during counseling without converting the association into deterministic treatment advice.

atomicClaims.statement: The 2022 ACC/AHA guideline recommends elective repair of an unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm at a maximum diameter of at least 5.5 cm in men or at least 5.0 cm in women, and trials of routine repair for smaller asymptomatic aneurysms did not demonstrate a survival benefit.
atomicClaims.limitation: Diameter is not the only management consideration; symptoms, growth, anatomy, operative risk, patient preference, and specialist assessment remain relevant. This claim is used only to bound distractors in the approved concept.
atomicClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm being evaluated for surveillance or elective repair.
